steps.title: Intent
in: The concern, in their words: a new rule to set, or the change to an existing guideline

steps.title: Auditor
steps.actor: AI: a single auditor, who holds the discussion with the human
in: Overview and guidelines whose scope overlaps the intent's. Selected by script, index first. Never the code
out: Delta: overlaps, contradicts, modifies, hole. Three fields per line: entry, consequence, proposed resolution. Empty if nothing to report
Proposed scope, drawn from the project vocabulary. To validate at the gate

steps.title: Challenge
steps.actor: Human T, opened by script only if the delta is not empty
in: The delta, short and in fixed form
On request: a question to the auditor about a line of the delta
out: Revised intent, back to the audit
The auditor's answer, read-only, quoting the entry concerned. It modifies no document: only a revised intent has an effect

steps.title: Writer
out: Proposed guideline, or overview update: the rule, its reason in a few lines, what it replaces, how to verify it (linter, test, build or judgment), its scope. New guideline: a file created at `guidelines/<id>.md`. Existing entry: that same file, same id

steps.title: Validator
steps.actor: Persona distinct from the lead: it receives the deliverable alone, never the discussion

steps.title: Code checks
out: Valid schema, scope present and from the vocabulary, cited identifiers exist, each statement cites its source, ambiguous words, verification filled in, no scope overlap with an accepted guideline without "replaces"

steps.title: Judge
steps.actor: AI, four fixed questions, citation required

questions.q: Is each sentence of the intent carried?
Is a statement unsupported by its cited source?
Is there a contradiction with a cited guideline?
Do two statements contradict each other?

out: Yes or no, with citation: is each sentence of the intent carried? a statement unsupported by its cited source? contradiction with a cited guideline? two statements contradicting each other?

steps.title: Gate 1 · Review
in: Code checks and judge, all green
out: Text and scope validated. The guideline stays proposed until the rule is merged
Or changes: back to the intent

steps.title: Implementer
in: Validated guideline, and the guidelines and tooling whose scope overlaps its own
out: Linter, test or build constraint, limited to the guideline's scope
Examples that must pass and that must fail
Configuration in architecture/ and the project

steps.title: Implementer's question
steps.actor: Human T, only if the implementer is blocked: answers its question
in: Card: the blocking point, the options with their effect and cost, the recommendation
out: Answer, recorded in the rule's documents. Implementation resumes

steps.title: Validator
steps.actor: Persona distinct from the lead: it receives the deliverable alone, never the discussion
out: List of defects, free critique: does the rule do what the guideline says?

steps.title: Code checks and case file
out: Each statement covered by a rule or marked "judgment", each rule tied to a statement, examples ok, non-empty rule (injected violation detected)
One-page case file: replay on history (changes that would have been blocked), existing violations per folder

steps.title: Judge

questions.q: Do the examples illustrate the statement?

out: Yes or no: do the examples illustrate the statement?

steps.title: PR opening and CI
in: Code checks and judge, all green
out: Pull request opened without agent review: the diff and the reports in the description. The CI runs on it
CI green on the PR: the script waits for the result. The merge happens only after the gate

steps.title: Gate 2 · Verification
in: Statement coverage, including those left at "judgment"
out: Merge: the guideline moves to status accepted and the rule becomes active
If violations are tolerated: frozen baseline list of existing violations
If remediation work: new technical need, Plan workflow (entry 2)
Or rejection: rule too broad or too narrow, back to the implementer. Wrong decision, back to the intent

steps.title: Accepted · merge
out: PR merged by script, after the gate
Guideline accepted in architecture/, with its scope

contract: A technical concern: debt, incident, new constraint, stack evolution, non-functional requirement (performance, security, accessibility), new scope to define, a repeated local ADR (promotion), or the change or acceptance of an existing guideline.
A guideline accepted in architecture/ and a rule active in CI.
Human T, at both gates. No human F.
notes: A script opens it only if the auditor's delta is not empty. Otherwise writing follows directly. The discussion is a loop between the human and the auditor, with no maximum number of rounds: at each round, the auditor receives the delta and the messages exchanged since its last round.

It only serves to get the CI to run before main, because the rule will block all following PRs. The code was already reviewed by the validator, and the human validates the case file at the gate. The merge happens after the gate.
Defining or modifying it is a decision of this workflow, with a gate: front, back, mobile, or any other split of the project.

Performance, security, accessibility are technical decisions: human T sets them alone here, with a verifiable rule (performance budget, automatic accessibility check). Each build applies them through the frame rules.
A durable rule for all future code belongs to this workflow. Bringing existing code into compliance belongs to Plan, entry 2.
Only workflow where the audit ignores the code
The intent is cross-cutting: it is confronted with decisions already made, not with the state of the code.
A decision without verification is refused by the format. "Judgment" is allowed, but listed at gate 2.
It adds to the examples, the non-empty rule and the replay on history. The control protocol, meaning when and how many rounds, will be defined later.
A guideline's reason is carried by the guideline itself. Discarded alternatives are not kept for now.
doc.lede: The technical frame is how the code is built: stack, structure, guidelines and the decisions behind them. A human T sets a technical decision that depends on no need. It becomes a guideline and a rule verifiable in CI.
